Hi Kayla —

Short answer: yes, we can support stacking in most cases, but there are a couple of operational and policy considerations. I’m looping in Ben (sales) and Laura (finance/ops) to confirm acceptable guardrails and any reporting options. High-level notes for you: 

- Stacking: We can apply multiple credit buckets to a single account if the account is enrolled via the cohort onboarding flow; sponsor credits are applied first by redemption voucher, then Rocket onramp credits apply to remaining usage.
- Expiration: Sponsor vouchers often have a 12-month expiry; onramp credits from Rocket are typically 9 months. If you need uniform expiry we can set sponsor vouchers to match, but that requires a sponsor agreement addendum.
- Usage covenant & reporting: We can emit redemption and token-usage reports at the cohort level. Laura — what cadence/fields can we commit to?

Can you confirm whether the sponsor insists on cohort-level names/emails in the report (PII) or if aggregate consumption is sufficient? If they require PII we’ll need a written data-sharing consent from founders and likely add a clause to the SOW.

I’ll follow up after hearing from Ben/Laura with a proposed contract clause and a short ops runbook.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: usage-covenant-template.docx

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Onramp grant question: can sponsor credits stack with our cohort voucher?

Sergio / Laura —

We can make a standard exception for stacking for accelerator-cohort flows. A few items we should confirm before we commit: 

1) Sponsor voucher redemption mechanism — is this a one-time voucher code per startup or a pooled sponsor account we manage? One-time voucher is easiest for us; pooled accounts add complexity around allocation and refund handling.
2) Expiry alignment — if sponsor insists on 12 months but Rocket onramp is 9 months, we should present two options to Kayla: (A) align sponsor to 9 months (preferred operationally) or (B) keep both expiries but mark sponsor voucher as first-draw and provide a 90-day post-grant reconciliation report.
3) Reporting fields — we can provide: account name, account id, total tokens consumed, percent used vs initial allocation, and dates of first/last usage. We need explicit consent for email/user-level exports. Aggregate CSV is fine without PII.
4) Billing/playback — any unused sponsor credits that expire are non-refundable. If Rocket wants to convert unused vendor credits to a multi-month extension, that’s a custom ops change.

If Kayla wants the sponsor to see founder-level redemption, we should ask for sponsor to sign our data sharing addendum (I’ll attach a suggested clause). Happy to approve stacking for this cohort if Kayla confirms voucher mechanism and reporting preference.

— Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Onramp grant question: can sponsor credits stack with our cohort voucher?

Ben/Serge —

From an ops and revenue recognition perspective we can support stacking but require: 
- Voucher metadata tracked as tags on the account (sponsor:voucher_id, cohort:onramp_id) so we can split redemption for audit.
- Expiry policy documented in SOW; different expiries okay but both must be explicit so founders understand.
- Reporting cadence: we can deliver a CSV summary at 30/90 days. If sponsor wants weekly updates that’s a billable ops engagement.
- Data sharing: PII exports need signed consent and legal approval (we’ll route a data-sharing addendum).

I’ve added the voucher metadata and reporting clause to the usage-covenant-template.docx (attached) — feel free to send to Kayla as the baseline.

Laura
Revenue Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
